person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A REGISTER OF WHICH NAMES HAVE LEGAL STANDING, PAIRED WITH A SERVICE THAT DECIDES CLASSIFICATION FROM A GENOME - the List of Prokaryotic names with Standing in Nomenclature and the Type (Strain) Genome Server, run as one interconnected pair at the DSMZ
span.quote: The List of Prokaryotic names with Standing in Nomenclature (LPSN) is an expert-curated authoritative resource for prokaryotic nomenclature and is available at https://lpsn.dsmz.de . The Type (Strain) Genome Server (TYGS) is a high-throughput platform for accurate genome-based taxonomy and is available at https://tygs.dsmz.de .

span.label: how to keep a nomenclature register and a genome-based classifier in step when names are proposed faster than they are validated and 99% of the organisms have no valid name at all
span.quote: The global prokaryotic diversity is estimated to encompass 0.8–1.6 million species ( 1 ) of which currently only about 1% ( 2 ) have a name that is validly published under the International Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes (ICNP) ( 3 ). Even though these estimates are likely to fluctuate, microbial life still remains largely unknown and unconnected to the only system of nomenclature accepted by the majority of microbiologists, the ICNP.

span.label: an expanded LPSN that now lists names WITHOUT standing and marks them as such, an API and CSV export for both platforms, and TYGS improvements for choosing the closest type strains
span.quote: An even more fundamental advantage of including not validly published names is that it adds clarity. If a name is shown on LPSN and explicitly marked as not being validly published, this leaves no doubt with regard to its status, as opposed to just not showing the name at all.

span.label: method
span.quote: To improve the coverage, a web form for submission was added to LPSN that allows for anonymous suggestions of taxon names. Synonymy relationships between taxon names and assignments of child taxa to parent taxa (i.e, genera to families, families to orders etc.) can also be suggested. The inclusion criterion is the presence of an effective publication as defined by the ICNP ( 3 ).

span.label: a code under which a name either is or is not validly published, applied to a domain where the naming rate is rising, the geography of naming is shifting and the type material itself is under debate
span.quote: Classification in turn needs an internationally accepted system of nomenclature to unambiguously assign names to taxa ( 3 ). The cornerstone of the ICNP is the status of taxon names as being validly published; other names have no claim to recognition under this code

span.label: expert curation plus automated import, with an inclusion criterion stated as a rule of the code rather than as an editorial judgement
span.term: expert curation plus automated import, with an inclusion criterion stated as a rule of the code rather than as an editorial judgement
span.quote: To improve the coverage, a web form for submission was added to LPSN that allows for anonymous suggestions of taxon names. Synonymy relationships between taxon names and assignments of child taxa to parent taxa (i.e, genera to families, families to orders etc.) can also be suggested. The inclusion criterion is the presence of an effective publication as defined by the ICNP ( 3 ).

span.label: **A NAME EITHER HAS LEGAL STANDING OR IT HAS NONE, AND 99% OF THE ORGANISMS HAVE NONE**: `The global prokaryotic diversity is estimated to encompass 0.8-1.6 MILLION SPECIES of which currently ONLY ABOUT 1% have a name that is VALIDLY PUBLISHED under the ICNP` - and `The cornerstone of the ICNP is THE STATUS OF TAXON NAMES AS BEING VALIDLY PUBLISHED; OTHER NAMES HAVE NO CLAIM TO RECOGNITION UNDER THIS CODE.` The corpus holds committees that vote and codes that classify; **this is a code that confers a STATUS, and the status is binary**
span.quote: The global prokaryotic diversity is estimated to encompass 0.8–1.6 million species ( 1 ) of which currently only about 1% ( 2 ) have a name that is validly published under the International Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes (ICNP) ( 3 ). Even though these estimates are likely to fluctuate, microbial life still remains largely unknown and unconnected to the only system of nomenclature accepted by the majority of microbiologists, the ICNP.

span.label: **AND THE REGISTER NOW LISTS THE NAMES THAT HAVE NO STANDING, BECAUSE ABSENCE IS AMBIGUOUS**: `An even more fundamental advantage of including not validly published names is that IT ADDS CLARITY. IF A NAME IS SHOWN ON LPSN AND EXPLICITLY MARKED AS NOT BEING VALIDLY PUBLISHED, THIS LEAVES NO DOUBT WITH REGARD TO ITS STATUS, AS OPPOSED TO JUST NOT SHOWING THE NAME AT ALL.` **A working solution to `an empty state is not an instance`** - the difference between a name that failed and a name nobody entered, made visible on the page
span.quote: An even more fundamental advantage of including not validly published names is that it adds clarity. If a name is shown on LPSN and explicitly marked as not being validly published, this leaves no doubt with regard to its status, as opposed to just not showing the name at all.

span.label: AND THEY CAMPAIGN ON IT: `The storage of not validly published names in LPSN ALLOWS FOR CONDUCTING CAMPAIGNS TO INCREASE THE RATE OF VALIDATION. As of July 2021, ALMOST 900 E-MAILS WERE SENT to corresponding authors to inform them about names proposed by them that AS YET HAVE NO CLAIM TO RECOGNITION under the ICNP, COVERING >1500 NAMES.` A register that writes to the authors of the rows it holds
span.quote: The storage of not validly published names in LPSN allows for conducting campaigns to increase the rate of validation. As of July 2021, almost 900 e-mails were sent to corresponding authors to inform them about names proposed by them that as yet have no claim to recognition under the ICNP ( 3 ), covering >1500 names.

span.label: AND STANDING CAN BE LOST RETROSPECTIVELY, AND MANY AUTHORS DO NOT KNOW IT EXISTS: `many names with an effective publication outside IJSEM ARE VALIDATED AT A LATER DATE anyway ... Conversely, NAMES SUPPOSED TO BE VALIDLY PUBLISHED MAY LATER ON BE RECOGNIZED AS NOT HAVING MET THE NECESSARY REQUIREMENTS. Moreover, NOT ALL TAXONOMIST ARE AWARE OF THE NEED FOR VALIDATION.` The status moves in both directions and is not self-announcing
span.quote: For instance, many names with an effective publication outside IJSEM are validated at a later date anyway ( 3 ), hence their earlier consideration facilitates data analysis. Conversely, names supposed to be validly published may later on be recognized as not having met the necessary requirements ( 32 ). Moreover, not all taxonomist are aware of the need for validation

span.label: **AND THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS PUBLISHED BESIDE THE NAME**: `comments about THE CONDITIONS UNDER WHICH A NAME WOULD BE REGARDED AS THE CORRECT NAME IF IT IS NOT CURRENTLY SO REGARDED by LPSN. The latter change is supposed to improve the understanding of THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN NOMENCLATURE AND CLASSIFICATION, WHICH MAY PUZZLE MANY MICROBIOLOGISTS.` A `holds_when` field in the wild - the row states what would have to be true for its own verdict to change
span.quote: Comments on taxonomic terminology were added to LPSN for single taxon names where appropriate, as well as comments about the conditions under which a name would be regarded as the correct name if it is not currently so regarded by LPSN. The latter change is supposed to improve the understanding of the difference between nomenclature and classification, which may puzzle many microbiologists ( 35 ).

span.label: AND THE NAME IS ANCHORED TO A PHYSICAL SPECIMEN, PERMANENTLY: `THE NOMENCLATURAL TYPE IS THE ENTITY WITH WHICH A TAXON NAME IS PERMANENTLY ASSOCIATED. In the cases of prokaryotic species and subspecies, the nomenclatural type IS THE TYPE STRAIN. CULTURES OF TYPE STRAINS THUS FIRMLY CONNECT TAXON NAMES AND GENOME SEQUENCES.` Our anchors point at a span of text; theirs point at a living culture in a collection
span.quote: The nomenclatural type is the entity with which a taxon name is permanently associated ( 3 ). In the cases of prokaryotic species and subspecies, the nomenclatural type is the type strain. Cultures of type strains thus firmly connect taxon names and genome sequences. Quality-checked ( 17 ) genome and proteome sequences of verified type strains are the starting point of TYGS analyses.

span.label: **AND AN ATTEMPT TO LET A GENOME BE THE ANCHOR FAILED**: `While A RECENT ATTEMPT TO MODIFY THE ICNP TO ALLOW FOR USING GENOME SEQUENCES AS NOMENCLATURAL TYPE WAS UNSUCCESSFUL, alternative solutions to the perceived underlying problem ARE CURRENTLY ACTIVELY DEBATED.` The question of WHAT MAY SERVE AS THE ANCHOR OF A NAME, put to a vote and rejected - and the consequence is that a species with no cultivable strain cannot be named at all
span.quote: While a recent attempt to modify the ICNP to allow for using genome sequences as nomenclatural type was unsuccessful ( 39 ), alternative solutions to the perceived underlying problem are currently actively debated ( 40 ).

span.label: AND THE INCLUSION CRITERION IS A RULE OF THE CODE RATHER THAN AN EDITORIAL JUDGEMENT: `a web form for submission was added to LPSN that ALLOWS FOR ANONYMOUS SUGGESTIONS of taxon names ... THE INCLUSION CRITERION IS THE PRESENCE OF AN EFFECTIVE PUBLICATION AS DEFINED BY THE ICNP.` Anonymous submission with a code-defined gate: **who proposes is unrestricted, what qualifies is not**
span.quote: To improve the coverage, a web form for submission was added to LPSN that allows for anonymous suggestions of taxon names. Synonymy relationships between taxon names and assignments of child taxa to parent taxa (i.e, genera to families, families to orders etc.) can also be suggested. The inclusion criterion is the presence of an effective publication as defined by the ICNP ( 3 ).

span.label: AND ONE GROUP IS GOVERNED BY TWO CODES AT ONCE: the register adds `names of CYANOBACTERIA VALIDLY PUBLISHED UNDER THE ICN (International Code of Nomenclature FOR ALGAE, FUNGI AND PLANTS), IN ANTICIPATION OF THE RECENT CHANGES TO THE ICNP` - so a name's standing depends on which code you ask, and the register has to hold both answers
span.quote: A major change regarding the selection of taxon names for inclusion in LPSN is the addition of names that are not validly published ( Candidatus names and other names), as well as of names of Cyanobacteria validly published under the ICN (International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi and plants), in anticipation of the recent changes to the ICNP ( 29 ).

span.label: **AND THE RIVAL INDEX IS INCONSISTENT WITH ITSELF ACROSS IMPLEMENTATIONS**: `the dDDH approach was shown to OUTPERFORM the `AVERAGE NUCLEOTIDE IDENTITY` (ANI) approach ... More recently, `ANI` WAS FOUND TO YIELD RESULTS THAT ARE INCONSISTENT ACROSS ITS VARIOUS IMPLEMENTATIONS DUE TO A LACK OF STANDARDIZATION.` One named measure, several programs, different numbers - **a species boundary that depends on which implementation you ran**
span.quote: As noted earlier, the dDDH approach was shown to outperform ( 18 , 19 ) the ‘average nucleotide identity’ (ANI) approach, which is also frequently used in scientific studies as an alternative OGRI index ( 5 ). More recently, ‘ANI’ was found to yield results that are inconsistent across its various implementations due to a lack of standardization ( 38 ).

span.label: AND A NEIGHBOURING RESOURCE'S BREADTH IS ITS HAZARD: `other platforms such as EzBioCloud may provide access to A BROADER SELECTION OF `REFERENCE GENOMES`, INCLUDING NON-TYPE STRAINS, these are to the best of our knowledge FREQUENTLY CONFUSED OR MISINTERPRETED AS TYPE STRAINS and may thus LEAD TO TAXONOMIC MISINTERPRETATIONS.` A category error made possible by a database that does not mark the distinction the code turns on
span.quote: Even though other platforms such as EzBioCloud ( 37 ) may provide access to a broader selection of ‘reference genomes’, including non-type strains, these are to the best of our knowledge frequently confused or misinterpreted as type strains and may thus lead to taxonomic misinterpretations.

span.label: **AND THE MACHINE-READABLE EXPORT IS SCOPED BY A SUPERSEDED SPREADSHEET**: `The LPSN CSV file NEEDED TO BE DOWNWARDS COMPATIBLE WITH THAT EXCEL FILE as far as possible, hence it was and is INTENDED TO CONTAIN ONLY THE NAMES OF GENERA, SPECIES AND SUBSPECIES VALIDLY PUBLISHED under the ICNP.` **So the download excludes exactly the not-validly-published names the website added for clarity** - a reader sees the absence marked and a program does not, and the reason is a format from a service that no longer exists
span.quote: The LPSN CSV (comma-separated values) file became available for download once LPSN was established at DSMZ ( 2 ). An Excel file was previously offered by the PNU (Prokaryotic Nomenclature Up-to-date) service of DSMZ, which was superseded by the new LPSN. The LPSN CSV file needed to be downwards compatible with that Excel file as far as possible, hence it was and is intended to contain only the names of genera, species and subspecies validly published under the ICNP.

span.label: THE COVERAGE OF NAMES WITHOUT STANDING CANNOT BE COMPLETE, AND THEY SAY WHY: `Because they are NOT CENTRALLY COLLECTED IN A JOURNAL such as IJSEM, THE COVERAGE OF NAMES BY LPSN THAT HAVE AN EFFECTIVE PUBLICATION BUT ARE NOT VALIDLY PUBLISHED UNDER THE CODE CANNOT BE EXPECTED TO BE COMPLETE. LPSN attempts to focus on NAMES THAT ARE IN USE, i.e. are found in the literature or in other databases.` The invalid half of the register is a convenience sample of what people actually write
span.quote: To improve the coverage, a web form for submission was added to LPSN that allows for anonymous suggestions of taxon names. Synonymy relationships between taxon names and assignments of child taxa to parent taxa (i.e, genera to families, families to orders etc.) can also be suggested. The inclusion criterion is the presence of an effective publication as defined by the ICNP ( 3 ).

span.label: AND THE GROWTH IS IN THE DATA, NOT IN THE UNDERSTANDING: `the overall number of names that become validly published per year SHOWS AN EVER-INCREASING TREND. ONE OF THE CHALLENGES OF NOMENCLATURE-RELATED DATABASES IS APPARENTLY THE SHEER INCREASE OF THE VOLUME OF THE DATA TO BE CONSIDERED` - against 1% of estimated species named at all, so the rate rises while the fraction barely moves
span.quote: The number of validly published names per country and year reflects the well-known shift of taxonomic activity to East Asian nations ( 28 ). The relative and absolute number of emendations also shows an increasing trend, caused by the availability of genome sequences of type strains ( 8–11 ). More importantly, the overall number of names that become validly published per year shows an ever-increasing trend. One of the challenges of nomenclature-related databases is apparently the sheer increase of the volume of the data to be considered.

span.label: AND THE SCALE IS SMALL AGAINST THE DOMAIN: `the LPSN database provides ... >26K NAMES of any category and >21K SPECIES NAMES validly published under the ICNP ... the TYGS database contains >15K TYPE-STRAIN GENOMES.` Twenty-one thousand named species against an estimated 0.8-1.6 million
span.quote: As of July 2021, the LPSN database (Figure 1 ) provides a large variety of expert-curated nomenclatural data, including >26k names of any category and >21k species names validly published under the ICNP ( 3 ). At the time of writing, the TYGS database (Figure 1 ) contains >15k type-strain genomes and was used by >3.7k different users worldwide for conducting >27k distinct analyses (Figure 2 ) involving 15M + genome comparisons.

span.label: AND THE TWO PLATFORMS ARE ONE INSTITUTION'S: both LPSN and TYGS are run at the Leibniz Institute DSMZ by the same four authors, and the paper's own recommendation is to migrate users off the earlier GGDC tool onto TYGS. The register of what counts as a name and the service that supplies the evidence for classification share a roof
span.quote: The List of Prokaryotic names with Standing in Nomenclature (LPSN) is an expert-curated authoritative resource for prokaryotic nomenclature and is available at https://lpsn.dsmz.de . The Type (Strain) Genome Server (TYGS) is a high-throughput platform for accurate genome-based taxonomy and is available at https://tygs.dsmz.de .

span.term: **A BINARY LEGAL STATUS, AND 99% OF THE ORGANISMS DO NOT HAVE IT**: `0.8-1.6 MILLION SPECIES of which currently ONLY ABOUT 1% have a name that is VALIDLY PUBLISHED`
span.quote: The global prokaryotic diversity is estimated to encompass 0.8–1.6 million species ( 1 ) of which currently only about 1% ( 2 ) have a name that is validly published under the International Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes (ICNP) ( 3 ). Even though these estimates are likely to fluctuate, microbial life still remains largely unknown and unconnected to the only system of nomenclature accepted by the majority of microbiologists, the ICNP.

span.quote: An even more fundamental advantage of including not validly published names is that it adds clarity. If a name is shown on LPSN and explicitly marked as not being validly published, this leaves no doubt with regard to its status, as opposed to just not showing the name at all.

span.quote: Comments on taxonomic terminology were added to LPSN for single taxon names where appropriate, as well as comments about the conditions under which a name would be regarded as the correct name if it is not currently so regarded by LPSN. The latter change is supposed to improve the understanding of the difference between nomenclature and classification, which may puzzle many microbiologists ( 35 ).

span.quote: The LPSN CSV (comma-separated values) file became available for download once LPSN was established at DSMZ ( 2 ). An Excel file was previously offered by the PNU (Prokaryotic Nomenclature Up-to-date) service of DSMZ, which was superseded by the new LPSN. The LPSN CSV file needed to be downwards compatible with that Excel file as far as possible, hence it was and is intended to contain only the names of genera, species and subspecies validly published under the ICNP.

span.quote: Classification in turn needs an internationally accepted system of nomenclature to unambiguously assign names to taxa ( 3 ). The cornerstone of the ICNP is the status of taxon names as being validly published; other names have no claim to recognition under this code

span.label: `THE ENTITY WITH WHICH A TAXON NAME IS PERMANENTLY ASSOCIATED` - for prokaryotic species and subspecies, the type strain
span.term: nomenclatural type
span.quote: The nomenclatural type is the entity with which a taxon name is permanently associated ( 3 ). In the cases of prokaryotic species and subspecies, the nomenclatural type is the type strain. Cultures of type strains thus firmly connect taxon names and genome sequences. Quality-checked ( 17 ) genome and proteome sequences of verified type strains are the starting point of TYGS analyses.
